title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 13 August 2026 (week 33) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: Published 13 August 2026; data period up to week 32 (3–9 August 2026).
analysis.location_and_population: Touch device users, explore by touch or with swipe gestures.
analysis.event: Weekly national surveillance report summarizing COVID-19 activity caused by SARS-CoV-2, issued by the UK Health Security Agency.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: COVID-19 activity increased across indicators and is circulating at baseline levels; SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity in hospital settings rose to 2.2% (week ending 9 August 2026) from 1.6% the prior week; overall weekly hospital admission rate for COVID-19 increased to 0.25 per 100,000 from 0.19 per 100,000; ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness remained low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Report notes baseline circulation and does not indicate heightened risk; data are provisional and subject to retrospective updates; surveillance systems monitor SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and other seasonal respiratory viruses.

analysis.brief_en: England’s weekly national surveillance report for week 33 (13 August 2026) shows COVID-19 activity driven by SARS-CoV-2 rising to baseline levels. SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity in hospital settings reached 2.2% for the seven days ending 9 August, up from 1.6% the previous week, while the overall weekly hospital admission rate climbed to 0.25 per 100,000 from 0.19 per 100,000. Emergency department visits for COVID-19-like illness stayed low. The UK Health Security Agency report, based on data through 9 August, classifies current COVID-19 activity as baseline and notes that surveillance indicators for influenza and RSV remain at baseline or low levels.
